mechanism_narrative: Sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility toward baseline indicates commuters are returning to offices, which increases weekday foot traffic around retail and recreation venues and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues to rise but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its mean over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT recovery crossing above -55% is a threshold signal that public transport is safe enough for discretionary trips, causing RETAIL_REC to rise over the next two weeks as shoppers return to stores.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -55% for at least one week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains above -55% but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility and rising TRANSIT jointly signal that people are leaving home and using public transport, a combination that amplifies retail and recreation visits and pushes RETAIL_REC higher over two weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL is below +13% and TRANSIT above -55% but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under phased de-escalation with regional border reopening, GROCERY_PHARM spending stabilizing near -2% marks the end of pantry stocking, freeing household budgets for discretionary retail and raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
regime_hint: phased de-escalation with regional border reopening
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays within 1 point of -2% but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Early-summer heat in Madrid reduces PARKS use by more than 8 points week-on-week, shifting outdoor recreation indoors to air-conditioned retail spaces and lifting RETAIL_REC over the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 8 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If PARKS falls more than 8 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC the next week is lower than the prior week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT creates a reinforcing mobility cycle that lifts retail and recreation activity, so RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks when both series recover together.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES above -25% and TRANSIT above -55% in the same week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both meet the thresholds but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent high RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with weakening PARKS use signals renewed caution and avoidance of public spaces, which depresses retail and recreation visits and drives RETAIL_REC lower over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above +12% and PARKS below -20% in the same week
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL is above +12% and PARKS below -20% but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES crossing above -25% marks a return of office-based work that increases after-work retail trips, causing RETAIL_REC to rise over the next week.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES is above -25% but RETAIL_REC the following week is not higher than the prior week, the hypothesis is rejected.
